finding.claim: getRedirectUrl does not neutralise a leading '/.' followed by '//', so a request path like /.//<dirname> yields a Location of //<dirname>/, a protocol-relative open redirect to the host named by an existing served directory. Conditional: requires redirect:true and an attacker-creatable directory named as a host in the served root.
finding.source: Raw request URL path, e.g. GET /.//evil.com (index.js:141-144 wildcard handler, prefix '/')
finding.sink: reply.redirect(getRedirectUrl(request.raw.url), 301) at index.js:319 (directory case) and index.js:157 (prefix route); Location header

trace.note: wildcard handler receives req; prefix '/' so matchRoutePrefix returns 0
getPathnameForSend(req.raw.url) returns '/.//evil.com' (no '..' segment so dotDot guard at 769 does not trigger)
pumpSendToReply dotDot check passes: no '..' segment
send resolves '/.//evil.com' to root/evil.com; a directory yields type 'directory'
leading-slash collapse only applies when url starts with '/' followed by '/' or '\\'; here url[1] is '.', so url stays '/.//evil.com'
new URL('/.//evil.com','http://localhost.com/').pathname === '//evil.com' (single-dot segment dropped, empty segment kept)

finding.guards_checked: Leading-'/'-collapse in getRedirectUrl only handles a run of slashes at the start of the URL; dotDotSegmentRegex (index.js:23) and getPathnameForSend dot-dot check (index.js:769) only reject '..' segments, not '.' followed by '//'; send's UP_PATH guard does not apply to '.'; no host or scheme allowlist exists on the redirect target. Not exploitable with an attacker-chosen host unless the attacker can create a directory in the served root (e.g. an upload feature that creates directories); the prefix redirect at index.js:155-159 is exact-match only and not affected.

finding.claim: _getExtendedInfo recurses into every directory found via fs.stat (which follows symlinks) with no visited-set or depth limit, so a symlink in the served tree that points to an ancestor makes each unauthenticated listing request walk an effectively unbounded, branching tree. Conditional: requires list.extendedFolderInfo: true and a symlink cycle in the served root (developer or repo content).
finding.source: Unauthenticated GET for a directory path that triggers listing (index.js:306-315 or 348/373 fallbacks) when the list option is enabled
finding.sink: dirList._getExtendedInfo recursion (lib/dirList.js:38-41), reached from dirList.list worker (lib/dirList.js:99-101)

trace.note: directory-type response with opts.list set calls dirList.send
for each subdirectory, if options.extendedFolderInfo, call getExtendedInfo(path)
fs.stat follows symlinks, so a symlink-to-ancestor reports isDirectory() true
recursion into filePath with no visited set and no depth cap; each level re-lists and re-stats every child

finding.guards_checked: Recursion is bounded only by the OS ELOOP/ENAMETOOLONG failure on deep symlink paths (~32-40 hops per resolution), which still allows large branching fan-out per request; no lstat, no realpath dedupe, no concurrency or time budget. The default list option is off, and the library's own glob at index.js:169 uses follow:true with cycle protection, which dirList does not replicate. Impact is CPU and fd exhaustion from one request; no data exposure.
